_note: Curated Book of Mormon names - see scripts/build_bom_names.py's docstring for the tiers and rules. Meanings and proposals are this project's own summaries; the build links each name's Onomasticon page. Add "people": "jaredite" for a Jaredite name.

proposals.meaning: my father is cast down
proposals.origin: Hebrew ʾāḇ, father (H1) + a root meaning to cast down - though that root isn't found in West Semitic names

proposals.meaning: my father be praised
proposals.origin: father (H1) + nʾd, to praise, found in Akkadian and Amorite names

proposals.meaning: the rock is my father
proposals.origin: Hebrew ʾeḇen, stone (H68) + ʾad, father (as in Ugaritic names)

proposals.meaning: compare the Old Akkadian name a-ba-na-da, the closest known ancient name

Abinadom.meaning: uncertain - perhaps "my father is a wanderer"

proposals.meaning: my father is a wanderer, or father of their wandering - fitting Jacob's "wanderers, cast out from Jerusalem" (Jacob 7:26), as John W. Welch notes
proposals.origin: Hebrew ʾāḇ, father (H1) + nûḏ, to wander (H5110)

proposals.meaning: my father is grieved
proposals.origin: the same root nûḏ, to show grief

proposals.meaning: my father repented

Abish.meaning: uncertain - perhaps "my father is a man"

proposals.meaning: father is a man, or father of man - women's names with "father" (Abigail, Abishag) are biblical
the same as a name ʾbšʾ on a seal from before 587 BC, whose meaning is unknown
proposals.origin: Hebrew inscription; compare the Bible's Abishai

proposals.meaning: meadow, pasture - as in the Bible's Abel place names and the Ugaritic "city of the meadows"
green meadows
mourning - less likely, since the vowels don't fit
compare the Aramean place Bit Agush (Arpad, in Syria)
toil, labor
crooked, perverse - a fitting name for a wilderness of bitter battles
proposals.origin: Hebrew ʿiqqēš, as in the Bible's Ikkesh (H6142)
proposals.proponent: Robert F. Smith and John A. Tvedtnes

proposals.meaning: perhaps another form of the same root as Akish, named nearby
brother - tempting, but only a guess for a Jaredite name
contains Kish, a Jaredite name - also a major city near Babylon
like the Philistine king Achish of Gath (1 Samuel 21:10), whose name is Aegean
crooked, perverse
proposals.proponent: Robert F. Smith and John A. Tvedtnes

proposals.meaning: the Egyptian-Hittite name for Cyprus
young man, or young man of God - the first Alma is introduced as "a young man" (Mosiah 17:2); "Alma son of Judah" appears in a 2nd-century Judean desert document
proposals.origin: Hebrew ʿelem, youth (H5958), with a short ending for God's name

proposals.meaning: lad of God - the same epithet given the hero of the Ugaritic Kirta epic
a possible play on "hidden" when Alma hides by the waters of Mormon (Mosiah 18:5)
the one from Malek, or kingly
proposals.origin: Semitic mlk, to rule; king (H4428), with a place prefix and the -i ending meaning "of"

proposals.meaning: the Amalekite - though it's hard to see why Nephites would name a son after a hated enemy
built on mlk, "king" (H4428), with -iah, a short form of Jehovah - which would make it the only such Nephite name
related to Amalek (H6002) - unlikely unless it was a name his enemies gave him
the command, or word - perhaps short for Amariah, "command of Jehovah"
proposals.origin: Hebrew ʾāmar, to say or command (H559), with the name ending -on

proposals.meaning: commander, overseer - with wordplays in Omni 1 and Jarom
worshipper
proposals.origin: Semitic ʿmr, to live or honor, as in the name Omri

proposals.meaning: people of fortune
proposals.origin: Semitic ʿam, people or kinsman (H5971) + gad, fortune (H1409)

proposals.meaning: my people, or my (divine) kinsman, is praised - Abinadi with "people" in place of "father"
proposals.origin: Hebrew ʿam, people or kinsman (H5971) + a root meaning to praise

proposals.meaning: people of my wandering
my paternal uncle is a nomad, or a preacher
contains the Egyptian god's name Amon

Amlici.meaning: uncertain - perhaps "I will reign" or "my kingship"

proposals.meaning: I will reign, or I have made a king - fitting a man who sought to be king (Alma 2:2)
proposals.origin: Hebrew mālaḵ, to reign (H4427), as a verb form

proposals.meaning: my kingship
proposals.origin: the same root as a noun

proposals.meaning: my messenger - a distant possibility
perhaps a spelling of Amaron - "the command"
speaker, wordsmith - a profession name, fitting for a record keeper
people of the ark - less likely
the name Ammon with the -hah ending of names like Nephihah - the city was named after its founder (Alma 8:7)
Jehovah is my faithfulness - if -ihah is God's name
Amon of battle - possible but unlikely
people of our lord, or the (divine) kinsman is our lord
proposals.origin: Hebrew ʿam, people or kinsman (H5971) + West Semitic mrʾ, lord

proposals.meaning: (God's) word or command
proposals.origin: Hebrew ʾāmar, to say (H559), with the name ending -on

proposals.meaning: people of the ark - possible but unlikely
my maker is fortune (or fate)
his faithfulness, or he is faithfulness - likely first a person's name, as places were named after people
proposals.proponent: Robert F. Smith and John A. Tvedtnes

proposals.meaning: contains the Egyptian god's name Amon - unlikely

Amoron.meaning: uncertain - a later form of Amaron or Ammoron

proposals.meaning: a late form of Amaron or Ammoron
he of Moron - like the Maya naming pattern "he of" a place
the Mulek - Mulek with a remnant of the article "the"
trouble, toil - the Bible's Amal with a name ending
proposals.origin: Hebrew ʿāmāl, toil (H5999); compare Amal, H6000

proposals.meaning: people of the lodging place - unlikely
people of the circumcision - unlikely, though apt for a priest who claimed strict keeping of the law
proposals.proponent: Robert F. Smith and John A. Tvedtnes

proposals.meaning: revealed spring, or rock spring
proposals.origin: Hebrew ʿayin, spring (H5869) + gālâ, to reveal (H1540) or gālal, to roll away a stone (H1556)

proposals.meaning: the printer's manuscript spells it Angolah; the 1830 edition, Angelah
perhaps a native place name, or Egyptian (compare names with ʿn.tj)
The element anti- appears in many Book of Mormon names; it may be Egyptian nty, "he of, the one who," or the Greek anti, "facing, against"
those who are (or are of) Nephi-Lehi
proposals.origin: Egyptian nty, "which is, the one of"

proposals.meaning: facing (toward) Nephi and Lehi
proposals.origin: Hebrew neḡeḏ, before or facing (H5048) - the word behind "help meet" in Genesis 2:18

proposals.meaning: those who imitate the teachings of the descendants of Nephi and Lehi
proposals.origin: English "anti" in its sense of "in place of, representing"

proposals.meaning: he of his faithfulness, one faithful to him
proposals.origin: Egyptian nty, he of + Semitic ʾmn, faithfulness (H539)

proposals.meaning: facing his faithfulness
proposals.origin: Greek anti, facing + the same ʾmn

proposals.meaning: one having a priestly office
proposals.origin: Egyptian nty, the one having + wnh, a kind of priest

proposals.meaning: one possessed of humility
a play on the antion, the gold coin (Alma 11:19) - "Mr. Gold Nugget," ruler of wealthy Ammonihah, alongside Zeezrom, "Mr. Moneybags"
place of gold - the antion was the most valuable Nephite coin, fitting the proud, wealthy Zoramite city
proposals.origin: antion + the old Semitic place ending -um, "at, in"

proposals.meaning: he who is there (in heaven) - for the general who fell at Cumorah
opposite the heifer - compare the biblical town Parah (Joshua 18:23)
who is Pharaoh, or which is the sun (Ra)
opposite side - much less likely
the same name as Antipas (Revelation 2:13) - see the Onomasticon's ANTIPAS entry
many waters, 10,000 waters - compare Irreantum, "many waters" (1 Nephi 17:5)
north of the narrow neck, so perhaps Jaredite or native
chief magistrate, or ruler - Greek titles spread through the eastern Mediterranean with traders and mercenaries
he of Zoram - like "he of Sinai" (Judges 5:5) and Zenephi, "he of Nephi"
proposals.origin: Hebrew zeh, this one, he of + Zoram

Chemish.meaning: uncertain - perhaps the god-name Chemosh, or "five"

proposals.meaning: the same as Chemosh, the Moabite god (1 Kings 11:7), also found as a personal name on a seal - one of many Book of Mormon names linked to the land east of the Jordan
five - perhaps as the fifth generation from Lehi
to arise, stand up - which can describe a hill or height
proposals.origin: Semitic qûm, to arise (H6965); Hebrew qômâ, height (H6967)
proposals.proponent: George Reynolds and Janne M. Sjodahl

proposals.meaning: to crush
the printer's manuscript spells it Comron; the 1830 typesetter swapped two letters. A hill, perhaps the masculine form of the same name as Cumorah
heap up (including heaps of the slain)
lion cub - matching his brother Shiblon's name (Arabic šibl, lion cub)
opponent, enemy
perhaps related to the Jaredite names Coriantum, Coriantor, and Coriantumr

Coriantor.meaning: uncertain - perhaps "child of the heavenly mountain"

proposals.meaning: heavenly-mountain child, or child of the east wind of heaven - only if Sumerian can explain Jaredite names
proposals.origin: Sumerian kur, mountain or east + an, heaven + tur, child

proposals.meaning: young lord, or young priest, as an alternative ending
something to do with a lion or cat - suggested for several Jaredite names, unconfirmed

Coriantumr.meaning: uncertain - perhaps "the heavenly mountain of god"

proposals.meaning: the heavenly mountain of god - only if Sumerian can explain Jaredite names
proposals.origin: Sumerian kur, mountain + an, heaven + dingir, god

proposals.meaning: something to do with a lion or cat - suggested for several Jaredite names, unconfirmed
a plant, or a hole or mine - highly doubtful
the same as Kurum, a Sumerian king of Uruk - judge, inspector
hidden away
(place of) cumin - less likely
the Jaredite element kumen, or Egyptian, as in Pacumeni
holy place, sanctuary
the Lord is hidden - an unlikely name for a child unless born at a hard time
proposals.origin: Hebrew kmn, to hide (in Aramaic, to lie in ambush) + -hah

proposals.meaning: compare Khamunira, a name in the Amarna letters
arise, O light (of the Lord) - the hill where Mormon hid the records that would come forth
proposals.proponent: David A. Palmer and Robert F. Smith

proposals.meaning: the Jaredites called the same hill Ramah (Ether 15:11) - Hebrew for a high place
place of inheritance - the text plays on it: "this land Jershon is the land which we will give unto our brethren for an inheritance" (Alma 27:22)
proposals.origin: Hebrew yāraš, to inherit or possess (H3423), with the place ending -ōn
proposals.proponent: John A. Tvedtnes and Jo Ann Hackett

proposals.meaning: land of the expelled, or of strangers - offered without a derivation
proposals.origin: perhaps Hebrew gāraš, to drive out

proposals.meaning: Kish, a biblical name (Saul's father), + kumen, an element shared with the Nephite names Kumen, Kumenonhi, Cumeni, and Cumenihah - so likely a Nephite name, not Jaredite
compare the Egyptian-Hittite city Kumani
a name from the Semitic root lmn - found as a personal name once, in an inscription from northwest Arabia (Lihyanite, mid-first millennium BC)
mender
evil, or scoundrel - less persuasive
surely he is faithful - intriguing, but doesn't fit the language
lord, or our lord
proposals.origin: West Semitic mrʾ (as in mrn, "our lord," in ancient Hatra)

proposals.meaning: like the Galilean town Meron and the biblical place behind "Meronothite" (1 Chronicles 27:30)
myrrh, the incense of South Arabia
rebellion - less likely
of Moron, belonging to Moron - named after the Jaredite land
lord, or our lord
my beloved, or I was beloved
(my) lord - less likely
the same root as Moron and Moroni, with the -hah ending common in Nephite names
Jehovah is (my) lord - less likely, since it would need an Aramaic word and a form of God's name not otherwise known that early
the Lord delivers, or saves - compare Isaiah, "the Lord is salvation"
proposals.origin: Hebrew môšīʿyāhū, from yāšaʿ, to save (H3467) + the short form of God's name (H3050)

proposals.meaning: deliverer - though this doesn't explain the final h
Messiah - though this doesn't give the o vowel
good, beautiful - perhaps echoed in "born of goodly parents" (1 Nephi 1:1); the name is attested in Egypt in Lehi's time
proposals.origin: Egyptian nfr (a final r is often dropped in late Egyptian)

proposals.meaning: the name of an Egyptian captain
to breathe, blow
proposals.proponent: John A. Tvedtnes and Jo Ann Hackett

proposals.meaning: the living one
proposals.origin: Egyptian p3-ʿnḫ, a common Egyptian name for over a thousand years

proposals.meaning: the same name as the Egyptian pharaoh Piankhi
the "paaneah" in Joseph's Egyptian name Zaphnath-paaneah (Genesis 41:45)
proposals.origin: Egyptian, as written in Hebrew, H6847

proposals.meaning: the Egyptian
proposals.origin: Egyptian p3-kmt, with the same "the" prefix (pa-) as Pahoran and Paanchi

proposals.meaning: like the names of Egypt's last priest-governors (Pa-menech, Pamenches)
blind man
-cumeni may be the Jaredite name element kumen (as in Kishkumen), which would make an Egyptian origin doubtful
the Syrian (Hurrian)
proposals.origin: Egyptian p3-ḥry; compare the Bible's Horites, H2752

proposals.meaning: the name of Egyptian officials in Canaan
proposals.origin: Canaanite paḥura, in the Amarna letters

proposals.meaning: governor
assembly, or potter

Sariah.meaning: prince of Jehovah, or Jehovah is prince

proposals.meaning: prince (or commander) of Jehovah, or the prince is Jehovah - the feminine of the Bible's Seraiah, found as a Jewish woman's name in the Elephantine papyri of Egypt
proposals.origin: Hebrew śar, prince (H8269) + yāh, the short form of God's name (H3050); compare Seraiah, H8304
proposals.proponent: Paul Y. Hoskisson and Stephen D. Ricks

Shazer.meaning: twisting, intertwining - perhaps the twisted acacia trees of an oasis campsite

proposals.meaning: to twist, to intertwine
pass of the trees - a common Palestinian place name
young gazelle - fitting the hunting there
gift, presentation
proposals.origin: like the Bible's Tubal (H8422), from yāḇal, to bring (H2986), with the Hebrew noun ending -oth

proposals.meaning: "curses are good" - a fitting slur for the family of an apostate king who started a long war
skilled (as a metalworker), after Tubal-cain, "instructor of every artificer in brass and iron"
seed of compassion, or merciful scattering
proposals.proponent: Jo Ann Hackett and John A. Tvedtnes

proposals.meaning: merciful scion (descendant) - shaped like Hebrew "royal seed" and the name Zerubbabel
proposals.origin: the same Hebrew words, read as a noun and participle

proposals.meaning: named like the Bible's Zerah, "(the Lord) has risen like the dawn"
arm of mercy - less likely, but perhaps a play on the name when Jesus says "arm of mercy" (3 Nephi 9:14) just after naming Zarahemla's destruction
